name: lab_conditions
label: Experimental conditions
description: How each experiment was run: setup, solvent, vessel, temperatures, pressure, pH, volumes, solid materials, controls, analysis, plus any other condition that could matter.
system_prompt: Extract the experimental conditions of a laboratory experiment paper. Report only what the paper states.
alternatives_rule: If the paper gives SEVERAL values of one condition for the same experiment from different methods (e.g. an oven set point and the temperature measured in the solution; a pH measured before and after adding a reagent), give each: the one the paper uses for its results without `meth`, every other one as its own entry with `meth` naming how it was obtained as the paper does, e.g. 'thermocouple in the solution'. A value that differs between experiments is NOT another estimate -- it belongs to its own set or sample.
open_ended_hint: e.g. light / UV irradiation, heating method, sealing or atmosphere details. Not the amounts of dissolved species or reagents (a separate step extracts those, when the data pack has it), and not the reaction time or sampling times (each row's duration is recorded already). Not ambient temperature or pressure, and not the controls, pH buffers, reagent suppliers, replicates or stirring / agitation (they have parameters)
intro: For every experiment set (and sample) in the structure plan below, extract the experimental conditions the paper reports. Conditions that are the same for every set go in ONE row with `set` ''; a condition that differs between sets goes in each set's row; one that differs between the samples of a set goes in each sample's row.

parameters.description: sealed or closed vessels heated in place, including wet-dry cycling and dry-downs in vials or on plates = Batch; continuous fluid flow through a stationary phase = Flowthrough. May be inferred from the described setup (a flask, vial or sealed tube = Batch): that counts as b 'derived', not assumed -- quote the setup.

how water figures in the reaction: Wet = in solution the whole time; Dry = a dry / solid-state reaction (no solution while it reacts); Wet-Dry = repeated hydration-dehydration (wet-dry) cycles; Drydown = a solution evaporated to dryness once, then heated / kept dry.

whether the reaction vessel was closed during the reaction: sealed = sealed ampoule or tube, capped or crimped vial, closed autoclave or bomb; open = open beaker or dish, reflux condenser open to air, evaporating on a plate. Only when the paper describes it (b 'derived' if read from the setup, e.g. 'sealed glass ampoules'); leave out for flow-through.
material of the reaction vessel, e.g. 'glass', 'PTFE', 'stainless steel'.

the solvent. For water, the type exactly as stated: distilled, deionized (DI), Milli-Q, ultrapure, nanopure, tap -- just 'water' if the paper doesn't say (the app then assumes distilled and flags it).

total volume of the reaction solution: as stated, or -- when the paper gives only the volumes of the solutions combined to make it -- their sum, with b 'derived' and the parts in `n` (the individual volumes are recorded with the chemistry).
how the products were analysed, briefly, e.g. 'HPLC (UV detection)', 'LC-MS'.
gas above the solution / atmosphere, e.g. 'N2', 'air', 'Ar'.
pressure at the start of the reaction.
pressure at which the samples were taken; for a pressurised reactor normally the reaction pressure (b 'derived' if the paper states it once).
reaction temperature (at the start).

temperature at which the samples were taken. When samples are taken at the reaction temperature, give it too (b 'derived' if the paper states the temperature only once per set) -- not just a note saying it's the same.
pH at the start, as set or measured before the reaction: per set or row when a table gives it (a 'pH' or 'starting pH' column of the conditions); a buffer's stated pH when the paper gives no other.
pH measured after the reaction or when the sample was taken: per row when a table of results gives it (a 'final pH' column, or a pH column among the results).

the solid present in the reaction, by its name -- a mineral, clay, solid catalyst or other material, e.g. 'montmorillonite', 'TiO2', 'CoFe2O4'; per set when the sets use different solids (also when another step records it as a catalyst); its kind goes in solid_material_type.
kind of solid, e.g. 'clay', 'oxide', 'sand'.
mass of that solid.
the positive control run alongside these experiments, briefly (at most 12 words: what it contained, e.g. '15 mM ImpA + 5-6 mg treated montmorillonite').
the negative control run alongside these experiments, briefly (at most 12 words, e.g. '15 mM ImpA, no mineral').
the pH buffer used, briefly (name and concentration, e.g. '50 mM HEPES, pH 7'), or 'none' when the paper says no buffer was used. Its pH also goes in initial_pH.
where the chemicals came from, briefly (suppliers, and purities if given, e.g. 'Sigma-Aldrich (>99%); minerals: Ward's Science').
how many times each experiment was run, as a whole number (in triplicate = 3, in duplicate = 2); how the replicates were combined (averaged, best of) goes in `n`.
how the solutions were mixed, stirred or agitated, briefly (e.g. 'magnetic stirring at 300 rpm', 'vortexed briefly, then left undisturbed'), or 'none' when the paper says there was none.

rules: sampled_temperature_C: give it for each set too -- the temperature the reaction was at when it was sampled or stopped; for heated reactions, dry-downs and wet-dry cycles that is the heating temperature -- normally the same value as initial_temperature_C, with b 'derived' if the paper states the temperature only once. Not the temperature of a quench, cooling bath or storage AFTER the reaction (faisal2005's effluent quenched at 5 °C: the sampled temperature is still the reactor's 240-300 °C; a quench goes in `other`). Don't leave it out just because it equals the reaction temperature. The same for sampled_pressure_bar when the reactor is pressurised (flow-through, autoclave): normally the reaction pressure, b 'derived' if stated once.

Leave out any condition the paper doesn't state -- never a typical or default value. The one convention: where the paper SAYS the experiments ran at ambient or room temperature ('r.t.'), give initial_temperature_C (and sampled_temperature_C) 25 with u '°C', b 'derived', n 'ambient temperature = 25 °C'; where it says ambient or atmospheric pressure, initial_pressure_bar 1 with u 'bar', b 'derived', n 'ambient pressure = 1 bar'. A temperature or pressure the paper gives for particular experiments wins for those experiments. Never put ambient conditions in `other`.

A value that needed a judgment call (e.g. a vessel material inferred from a device model) gets c 'medium' and the reason in `n`; if the paper states a condition twice with different values, give the one it uses and the other in `n`.

positive_control / negative_control: one short description per set; sets (or the whole paper, set '') that share the same controls get exactly the same wording, so they can be grouped. Leave them out when the paper describes no control.

A value with set '' is filled into EVERY row of the paper, including rows digitized later from its figures and appendix or supplementary experiments. When the paper says something holds for 'these experiments' but also reports experiments it doesn't cover (e.g. 'no pH buffers were used' and control experiments with organic pH buffers in an appendix), give the value with set '' and say in `n` which experiments are the exception ('except the pH-buffered controls, Appendix B').
